title: Somali (Ethiopia) Cambuulo
community: Ethiopian Somali communities — adzuki bean dessert
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Somali Cambuulo — adzuki beans slow-cooked until very soft, mixed with sesame oil and honey. The beloved Somali sweet-savoury bean dish eaten by Ethiopia's Somali communities — simultaneously a main dish and a dessert.
longDesc: Cambuulo is one of the most distinctive dishes of Somali food culture — the small adzuki beans cooked until completely tender, then dressed with sesame oil and honey. It is eaten both as a main dish (during Ramadan) and as a sweet at celebrations.
ingredients: 2 cups dried adzuki beans — soaked overnight
steps: Cook soaked adzuki beans 40—45 minutes until very tender.
Drain. While still warm, dress with sesame oil, honey, and cardamom.
chefTips: The beans must be very soft — almost melting.
Dress while warm — absorbs the oil and honey better.
cookingScience: Adzuki beans contain high concentrations of molybdenum (crucial for enzyme function) and are among the most digestible legumes.
sustainabilityTips: Adzuki beans fix nitrogen in soil.
culturalNote: Cambuulo is the sweet that the Somali diaspora carries with them everywhere — one of the most beloved comfort foods of Somali culture, appearing wherever Somali communities gather.
